title: Descent of finite relations among module maps
statement: Let I be a directed set and let (S_i)_{i\in I} be an inverse system of quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, where S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R_i) for Noetherian rings R_i, and let S=\varprojlim_i S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R). Let X_i be a finitely presented S_i-scheme [def-pc-scheme], put X=X_i\times_{S_i}S and X_j=X_i\times_{S_i}S_j for j\ge i [def-pc-base-change]. Fix a finite collection of finitely presented quasi-coherent \mathcal{O}_X-modules and maps between them, together with finitely presented models of those modules and maps on X_j whose base changes are identified with the given collection. If finitely many specified equalities between composites of the maps hold after base change to X, then, after replacing j by a later stage, all the specified equalities already hold on X_j.

source.place: Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR (finite relations among descended module maps)

proof.text: Replace the finite collection of modules and maps by the finitely many source and target modules and maps that occur in the specified composites. The statement already supplies finitely presented models on X_j with the prescribed base-change identifications; where a composite passes through a model only up to the identification, part (2) of the module-and-map descent statement, applied to the fixed models, lets us assume after increasing j that every map in every composite is a map between the chosen models, with the prescribed base-change identifications.

source.place: Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR (finite-presentation descent of modules and morphisms)

proof.text: Fix one specified equality and let \delta_j:F_j\to G_j be the difference of its two composites, an \mathcal{O}_{X_j}-linear map between finitely presented quasi-coherent models; pullback is additive and compatible with composition, so its base change to X is zero, and the same holds for its pullback \delta_{j'} to X_{j'} for every j'\ge j. Since X_i is of finite presentation over the affine S_i it is quasi-compact; choose a finite affine open cover U^1,\dots,U^n of X_i, U^a=\operatorname{Spec}A^a. Its inverse images in X_{j'} and X are the affine opens U^a_{j'}=\operatorname{Spec}B^a_{j'}, B^a_{j'}=A^a\otimes_{R_i}R_{j'}, and U^a_X=\operatorname{Spec}B^a, B^a=A^a\otimes_{R_i}R (fibre products of affines), and they cover. A map of sheaves vanishing on every member of an open cover vanishes; so it suffices to make \delta_{j'} vanish on each U^a_{j'} at one stage. (The Noetherian hypothesis on the R_i is not used anywhere in this proof; it is carried only because the citing setting has it.)

source.place: Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR (affine case plus Zariski glueing, first proof)

proof.text: Fix a. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] applied to the directed system (R_{j'})_{j'\ge i}, \operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim R_{j'}) with the induced maps is a limit of the system (S_{j'}); by uniqueness of limits it is identified with S=\operatorname{Spec}R compatibly with the projections, so, taking global sections, R=\varinjlim_{j'}R_{j'} as rings. Since A^a\otimes_{R_i}- commutes with colimits, B^a=\varinjlim_{j'\ge j}B^a_{j'}. On U^a_j the source F_j corresponds to a finitely generated B^a_j-module M with generators s_1,\dots,s_n, and the target G_j to a finitely presented B^a_j-module N=\operatorname{coker}(P:(B^a_j)^m\to(B^a_j)^p); the pullbacks to U^a_{j'} and U^a_X correspond to M\otimes B^a_{j'}, N\otimes B^a_{j'}=\operatorname{coker}(P\otimes B^a_{j'}) and similarly over B^a (right exactness of tensor product). Lift each \delta_j(s_k) to v_k\in(B^a_j)^p. Vanishing of the base change to X means that the image of v_k in (B^a)^p is P c_k for some c_k\in(B^a)^m. By clause (1) of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] for the directed set \{j'\ge j\} (a filtered category) and directedness, all finitely many entries of all c_k lift to some B^a_{j'}, giving \tilde c_k; each entry of v_k-P\tilde c_k\in(B^a_{j'})^p maps to 0 in B^a, so by clause (2) of the same statement (comparison with 0) it vanishes in some later B^a_{j''}, and by directedness one j'' serves for all of them. Then \delta_{j''}(s_k\otimes1)=0 for all k, and since the s_k\otimes1 generate M\otimes B^a_{j''}, \delta_{j''} vanishes on U^a_{j''}.

source.place: Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR (3), via Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-colimit-category-fp-modules

proof.text: There are finitely many affines U^a and finitely many specified equalities; by directedness choose one stage above all the stages found in the previous step. Vanishing on U^a_{j''} persists after pullback to any later stage, so at this common stage every difference map vanishes on every U^a, hence on X_j for the new j, i.e. all specified equalities hold on X_j.
